patterns.comment: Comment. Command definition source uses the CL form /* ... */, which may span lines.
patterns.name: comment.line.cmd

patterns.comment: Numeric literals, such as the length and decimal positions on LEN.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.cmd

patterns.comment: Special values, written with a leading asterisk.
patterns.name: constant.language.cmd

patterns.comment: A statement label. QUAL, ELEM and PMTCTL groups are named by a label and referred to by that name from a PARM.
patterns.name: keyword.control.cmd.label

patterns.comment: The six command definition statements: CMD, PARM, ELEM, QUAL, DEP and PMTCTL.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cmd

patterns.comment: Symbolic operators: concatenation, logical and relational. Written with a leading asterisk to distinguish them from names.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cmd

patterns.comment: Qualified name separator, as in MYLIB/MYPGM or *LIBL/QCMD. Matched before the arithmetic operators so a library qualifier is not scoped as division. CL division does not require spaces, so an unspaced &A/&B is scoped as a separator too; the reference writes division spaced, and qualified names are far commoner in practice.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.cmd

patterns.comment: Arithmetic, comparison and concatenation operators written as symbols.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cmd

patterns.comment: Quoted literal, such as prompt text or a special value's replacement.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.cmd

patterns.comment: Backslash escape inside a quoted literal. IBM i literals escape an apostrophe by doubling it rather than with a backslash, so this rule appears to be vestigial.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.cmd

patterns.comment: Parameter keyword, recognised by the parenthesis that follows it: KWD, TYPE, LEN, DFT and the rest.
patterns.name: support.function.cmd

patterns.comment: A CL variable reference, introduced by &.
patterns.name: variable.parameter.cmd
